text: Sixteen lessons ago, Finance wanted more than a one-time query. Here's what that turned into: a real transforming Glue ETL job, an actual modeled Redshift warehouse, a scheduled nightly refresh, two reports for two different stakeholders, and two realistic production bugs, fully diagnosed and fixed.

Northfield-orders-etl writing curated, partitioned Parquet into fact_orders and three real dimension tables. A repeatable COPY load, validated against source. A Spectrum path for queries that skip the warehouse entirely. EventBridge driving the whole nightly chain. Finance querying the warehouse, Ops querying Athena directly over curated data.

It would have been easy to skip the bugs and call this done. That's not real data engineering. A missing IAM permission, and a crawler silently misreading a schema change that never threw a single error. Reproduce, isolate the cause, confirm it, fix it, re-validate against the actual source. That discipline, calmly applied, is the real skill — not a detour from the build.

The Beginner project was raw files and ad hoc queries. This one added a transforming pipeline, a modeled warehouse, a schedule, two stakeholders, and two real bugs — genuine added scope and responsibility, not just more content.

The path's Advanced capstone takes this exact same pipeline further: Step Functions orchestration, CloudWatch monitoring and alerting, CI/CD for the Glue scripts, IAM hardening, and disaster recovery. Not a new scenario — the next, harder version of the exact same problem you just solved.
